newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swisslog sees higher sales, profits.
newsitem.headline: Swisslog sees higher sales, profits.

text.p: Swisslog Holding AG, which produces automated materials handling systems, said it plans to further improve its results this year and also exceed 400 million Swiss francs in sales.

However, Juhani Anttila, Swisslog chief executive, said in a statement that results in the logistics business in the first six months are normally lower than in the second half of the year and this "development is also likely in the current year."

Anttila said the profitability of Swisslog will be further enhanced this year by improving marketing efforts, development programmes for employees, broader geographical diversification, reduced order risks, stepping up customer support and the acquisition of Transnorm Systems and strategic alliances.
"Swisslog plans to move beyond the 400 million Swiss francs in total sales in 1997 and to further improve the results," Swisslog's statement said.
In 1996 Swisslog reported a net profit of 2.2 million francs compared with a loss of 3.89 million and operating profit improved to 7.2 million after an operating loss of 3.5 million.
Sales rose to 388.5 million francs from 255.8 million.
Swisslog directors will also propose to its shareholders on May 1 a capital repaymentof 34 francs per registered share by cutting the nominal value per share to 50 francs from 84 francs.
Subsequently, through a five-for-one split, the nominal value per share will be cut to 10 francs from 50.
